title: M10 Analysis and screenshot query (crux: statistics)
description:
- **Target:** yes for the screenshot and before/after prompts; the analysis is your extension. Files: `src/evaluate.py`, `src/plots.py`, `results/summary.json`.
- **Loops:** 75 queries; 2 comparisons x B resamples (B = 10,000 proposed; 20,000 resamples of 75 queries, seconds on a laptop); 24 per-type groups; 225 per-query rates.
- **Madi writes:** the bootstrap by hand (resample queries with replacement, average paired differences); stub and comments. Check against `scipy.stats.bootstrap` with paired samples. `uv add scipy` happens here.
- **Also:** per-type table with counts; Spearman rank correlation between greedy average logprob and acceptance rate per query.
- **Held decisions (ask with data):** B and interval level (proposal 10,000 and 95%, fixed seed).
- **Stated interpretation (please confirm):** the "screenshot rule" = pick the query with the largest GEPA improvement over the one-liner, ties going to the lower one-liner rate. I take this from the pitfall line; I have not seen the course text.
- **Read next to every number:** the independent unit is the query (75 test queries; the 20 draws are repeats). One query moves a mean difference by at most 1/75 = 1.3 points. Types with 2 to 3 test queries are descriptive only. Scores cover 300 of 541 IFEval prompts, so they are not comparable to published IFEval numbers.
- **Screenshot:** `make fig-summary` draws a forest plot of the two paired differences with bootstrap intervals (hand-written and SciPy overlaid) and a scatter of logprob vs acceptance rate with the rank correlation. One command prints the chosen query's one-liner output and GEPA output to the log, with pass/fail.
- **Tests:** (T28, edge case) a query missing from one prompt. (T29, edge case) the tie rule goes to the lower one-liner rate. (T30, edge case) groups with 2 or 3 prompts. (T31, behavior) fixed seed reproduces the interval. (T32, coupling guard) pairing by ID, not position (shuffle one side). (T33, coupling guard) IDs stay one type after a JSON round trip.

title: M9 Greedy outputs and logprobs (fast)
description:
- **Target:** your extension. Files: `src/evaluate.py`, `src/plots.py`, `results/greedy.json`.
- **Loops:** 3 prompts x 75 test queries = 225 greedy generations; reproducibility rerun on 10 queries x 3 prompts = 30. Estimate printed first.
- **How:** temperature 0, outside DSPy's LM call but with the same messages (`dspy.ChatAdapter().format(...)`), reply parsed with the same `ChatAdapter.parse` as M8; request `logprobs` on `/v1/chat/completions`.
- **I write** (non-crux): the average of the returned token logprobs over generated tokens only. She reviews it with before/after code and review questions.
- **Checks:** messages equal `lm.history[-1]["messages"]` for one live call; stop-token handling read on 3 outputs; logprob list length equals completion tokens. vLLM does not guarantee identical temperature-0 output across reruns (verified: docs.vllm.ai reproducibility page), so I report the diff count on the 30 reruns instead of asserting equality.
- **Screenshot:** `make fig-greedy` draws three panels (one per prompt): each query as a dot at its average logprob, coloured by pass or fail, so you can see whether confidence tracks passing.
- **Tests:** (T26, edge case) zero generated tokens does not divide by zero. (T27, measurement trap) the average covers generated tokens only.

title: M8 Test-set draws (crux: the final eval)
description:
- **Target:** partly. Files: `src/evaluate.py`, `src/plots.py`, `results/test_draws.json`.
- **Loops:** 3 prompts x 75 test queries x 20 draws = 4,500 generations (225 prompt-query cells, each flushed to disk). Estimate printed first, using M4's measured throughput. First time the test split is touched.
- **Layout:** results keyed by prompt name, then query ID; a crash resumes without redoing finished cells. Sampling settings saved; request failures counted apart.
- **Size:** about 4,500 responses at roughly 1.5 KB is several MB (assumed), over the 500 KB `check-added-large-files` limit, so `/results` stays gitignored.
- **Background:** `caffeinate -i`; frozen files: `assets/prompts.json`, `splits.json`, `config.py`, `evaluate.py`, and no redeploy of the server.
- **Screenshot:** the log's completion line, and `make fig-draws` draws a heatmap: rows = the 24 instruction types, columns = the 3 prompts, colour = mean pass rate, with 75-query overall bars beside it.
- **Tests:** (T23, coupling guard) results keyed by prompt and query ID. (T24, behavior) resume skips finished cells. (T25, measurement trap) settings saved; request failures counted apart.

title: M7 GEPA pilot run (crux)
description:
- **Target:** yes. Files: `src/optimize.py`, `assets/prompts.json`, `results/gepa.json`.
- **Loops:** about 740 student calls (4V + 380, V = 90) plus about 10 to 15 Gemini reflection calls (assumed). Estimate printed first; plan re-sent with real M4 and M6 numbers and approved before the run. Backgrounded.
- **Run:** `auto="light"`, Gemini as reflection model, `track_stats=True`, `log_dir`, `seed` recorded, train and validation passed by name.
- **Madi writes:** the GEPA constructor and `compile` call (stub and comments).
- **Record:** Gemini tokens (from the reflection LM's own `.history`; student and reflection LMs keep separate histories), Modal seconds, cost.
- **Decision here:** rerun with a raw cap (`max_metric_calls`) or not, after seeing the cost.
- **Screenshot:** `make fig-gepa` draws two charts: best validation score per candidate (from `detailed_results.val_aggregate_scores`), and bars for tokens, seconds and dollars by model. The one-liner and the GEPA instruction come from one printed log line.
- **Tests:** (T19, coupling guard) exactly one budget setting is set. (T20, behavior) saved instruction round-trips. (T21, edge case) counters sum across the two LMs. (T22, behavior) the seed is recorded.
- **Re-run invalidates:** the GEPA instruction and M8-M10. Archive, never overwrite (new run folder).

title: M6 GEPA metric and smoke run (crux)
description:
- **Target:** yes. File: `src/optimize.py`.
- **Loops:** 6 train prompts; budget held (shown with data below). Estimate printed first.
- **Madi writes:** `metric(gold, pred, trace=None, pred_name=None, pred_trace=None)` returning `dspy.Prediction(score=, feedback=)` (verified: GEPA raises TypeError unless it takes five positional args). Empty or unparseable reply gives 0 and a feedback message. I give the stub and comments.
- **Smoke:** tiny budget via `max_metric_calls`. Exactly one of `auto`, `max_full_evals`, `max_metric_calls` is set (verified: assertion in source).
- **Held decisions (ask with data):** `max_metric_calls` for the smoke (must exceed the first full validation pass plus one minibatch of 3); student temperature during GEPA (1.0 matches M8 but each score is noisy; 0 is steady but differs from what M8 measures); `num_threads` against server capacity (KV memory allows roughly 30 sequences of 2k tokens: arithmetic, assumed); whether to turn on `add_format_failure_as_feedback` (informed by the M4 parse-error rate; when False, failed-parse traces are dropped from reflection examples).
- **Screenshot:** log output of the smoke run (one round's scores, the feedback sent to Gemini, the new instruction); I compare it by eye to the course flow chart.
- **Tests:** (T17, edge case) the metric accepts the extra arguments; an empty reply scores 0 with feedback. (T18, coupling guard) the metric scores `pred.response`, not raw text.

title: M5 Baseline writer (fast)
description:
- **Target:** your extension. Files: `src/optimize.py`, `src/prompts.py`, `assets/prompts.json`.
- **Loops:** 24 train examples (one per type) go into 1 Gemini call. Estimate printed first.
- **What happens:** I write the meta-prompt (the instruction to Gemini: "here are 24 examples, one per type; write one general instruction") and keep it in `prompts.py`. Gemini `gemini/gemini-3.8-flash` (verified real) writes the baseline instruction. Nobody handwrites the baseline. Stated default: the example per type is the first train ID in sorted order.
- **Freeze:** `assets/prompts.json` stores the baseline plus a hash of the meta-prompt; a rerun refuses to overwrite it.
- **Screenshot:** log output: the printed baseline text and the writer's token and cost line.
- **Tests:** (T14, coupling guard) every example ID is in the train split. (T15, behavior) a second write is refused. (T16, edge case) empty reply and rate-limit error give a clear error (DSPy's `num_retries` handles retries; assumed).

title: M4 Pilot the one-liner (crux: headroom gate)
description:
- **Target:** supporting. Files: `src/evaluate.py`, `src/plots.py`, `results/pilot_oneliner.json`.
- **Loops:** smoke 3 prompts x 5 samples = 15 generations (read by hand first); full pilot 225 prompts x 5 samples = 1,125 generations. Estimate printed first.
- **Loop (Madi writes):** for one prompt, draw N = 5 samples at temperature 1.0 and average the passes (the acceptance rate). I give the stub and comments; sampling parameters are in vLLM's server docs.
- **Counts kept separate:** pass, fail, parse error (markers missing: scores 0 but tallied), request failure (not a fail; excluded from the denominator). Also saves wall-clock and completion tokens per call (feeds the estimate for M7 and M8).
- **Guard:** the function refuses the test split.
- **Decided before the run (stopping rule):** the cutoff for "piles up near 0% or 100%". I show the smoke rates and candidate cutoffs; she picks the number. With N = 5 rates move in steps of 20%.
- **Screenshot:** `make fig-pilot` writes a histogram of the 225 pass rates (bars at 0, 20, ... 100%), each bar split by train and validation colour, the stop-rule band shaded, parse-error share noted.
- **Tests:** (T11, measurement trap) aggregation on a fake result set with known answers; a failed request is not counted as a fail. (T12, edge case) all-pass, all-fail and a parse error. (T13, coupling guard) asking for the test split raises.

title: M3 Serve 3B on a T4, call it from DSPy (crux)
description:
- **Target:** supporting. Files: `src/modal_server.py`, `src/optimize.py` (LM setup only), `src/estimate.py`, `src/prompts.py`.
- **Loops:** 300 `/tokenize` calls (one per prompt, no generation); 1 DSPy call. Estimate printed before the call.
- **Server:** T4, `--dtype half` (verified: vLLM source rejects bf16 below capability 8.0), `--generation-config vllm`, `--api-key` from a Modal Secret, `--max-model-len` set from measured token length, `scaledown_window = 1200`, no `min_containers` (your choice). Model: `config.MODEL_NAME` (`unsloth/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct`).
- **Pins:** start from Modal's current example (`vllm==0.21.0`, `nvidia/cuda:12.9.0-devel-ubuntu22.04`, verified modal.com/docs/examples/vllm_inference); keep the versions the first successful run prints.
- **To probe (assumed):** which attention backend vLLM picks on a T4 (sm75). Run once with `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` and read the log. If startup fails twice I stop and explain.
- **Pre-GPU rule:** (1) token length: print the max of the 300 prompts plus template overhead plus `max_tokens`; (2) memory estimate with `kv_cache_mib(28, 8, 128, tokens)` plus 6.4 GB fp16 weights; (3) a 2-step probe through the real path (one call, then one through DSPy).
- **Madi writes:** the DSPy LM setup (`dspy.LM("openai/<served-name>", api_base, api_key, model_type="chat", temperature=1.0, cache=False)`) and one call to a one-line signature, then print `lm.history`. I give the stub with comments. The one-line signature and the one-liner text sit in `prompts.py` (I draft, she approves).
- **Verify by reading source:** DSPy 3.4.1 `ChatAdapter` retries with the JSON adapter when markers are missing (agent report, from a summarizer). That is a different prompt, so I configure fallback off and count parse errors as their own bucket.
- **Screenshot:** log output: `/v1/models` called with the key, and the printed `lm.history` for one call (shows where the instruction lands in the system message).
- **Tests (no Modal):** (T8, coupling guard) the vLLM command builder takes dtype, max-model-len and served name from `config`. (T9, measurement trap) a reply missing the markers is a fail, and the checker runs on the parsed `response` field, not raw text. (T10, behavior) the estimate sums by model.
- **Held decision (ask with data):** `MAX_NEW_TOKENS`. I print the largest "at least N words" requirement in the 300 kwargs and the longest prompt token count first.

title: M2 Checker and feedback (crux)
description:
- **Target:** supporting; defines GEPA's score and feedback. Files: `src/checks.py`, `src/prompts.py` (feedback template).
- **Loops:** 300 description builds, run twice to check determinism; 24 types x (1 passing + 1 failing) fixtures + 2 edge cases (empty, whitespace-only) = 50 checks. No LLM calls.
- **Wrapper (I write):** `passes(example, response) -> bool` calls the official strict check (verified: `evaluation_lib.test_instruction_following_strict` fails an empty or whitespace-only response). Feedback is one generic f-string kept in `prompts.py`: failed instruction id plus the instruction's own description text from the official class. I write it. No measured values and no per-type strings. If GEPA looks weak later, counts for a few types can be added.
- **Read first (together):** the official classes (`build_description`, `get_instruction_args`, `check_following`).
- **Default stated:** `langdetect.DetectorFactory.seed = 0` set once in `src/checks.py` (our code, not Google's); the official file never seeds it (verified by grep), so `response_language` (17 prompts) could flip between runs.
- **Checks:** determinism sweep on all 300; feedback exists only when the check fails; empty and whitespace-only fail with feedback.
- **Screenshot:** log output of one command that prints three failing responses (instruction id, a short excerpt, the feedback text).
- **Hand-checkable sample:** the 50 checks printed (type, response excerpt, pass/fail, feedback); wait for approval before M4.
- **Fixtures:** the official `instructions_test.py` keeps examples as literal strings inside test methods (assumed); I copy them into `tests/test_checks.py`. Offer: 8 representative types instead of 24 if it drags.
- **Tests:** (T5, behavior) feedback is not None iff `passes` is False, parametrized over the borrowed fixtures. (T6, edge case) empty and whitespace-only. (T7, coupling guard) feedback contains the instruction id.

title: M1 Load, filter, split (fast)
description:
- **Target:** supporting. Files: `src/data.py`, `src/plots.py`, `assets/splits.json`.
- **Loops:** 541 rows loaded, 305 single-instruction, 300 kept after dropping 1 type; 24 types; 2 sequential split calls.
- **Verified (agent pulled the data):** fields `key, prompt, instruction_id_list, kwargs`. Only `detectable_format:multiple_sections` (5) is at or below 6, so it is the one dropped type. Smallest kept type: `change_case:capital_word_frequency` with 7 prompts. Hand-derived split for it: 3/2/2 (assumed until M1 runs it). Expected totals about 135 / 90 / 75.
- **Rows keep:** `key`, `prompt`, the single instruction id, and `kwargs` with None-valued keys removed (verified: every dict has all 24 keys; 19,124 values are None).
- **I write** (non-crux): the stratified split, two sequential `train_test_split` calls (train 45% first, then the remaining 55% splits so validation is about 54.5% of it), `random_state=SEED`, `stratify` by type. She reviews it with before/after code and review questions.
- **Defaults stated:** `SEED = 42` (HW5 precedent); the drop rule is yours ("6 or fewer").
- **Checks:** sizes sum to 300; zero ID overlap; every type in all three splits; same seed gives identical IDs; `splits.json` round-trips with IDs one type.
- **Screenshot:** `make fig-split` writes a chart: one horizontal stacked bar per type (train / validation / test counts), types sorted by size, with the dropped type shown as a separate grey bar labelled "dropped".
- **Hand-checkable sample:** three types (smallest, mid, largest) printed with IDs and kwargs.
- **Tests:** (T1, edge case) a fake dataset with a 6-prompt type is dropped and a 7-prompt type lands 3/2/2; sweep n = 7..19 so a rounding change that empties a split fails. (T2, behavior) same seed same split; different seed differs. (T3, edge case) None-filter on real-shaped kwargs (row 1001 gives `{}`; a highlighted-sections row keeps `num_highlights`). (T4, coupling guard) saved split round-trips with IDs one type.

title: M0 Scaffold, config, deps (fast)
description:
- **Target:** supporting. Stay on the current branch.
- **Loops:** none.
- **Delete (after the reuse search):** `src/benchmark.py`, `guidance_html.py`, `html.py`, `methods.py`, `schema.py`, their five `tests/test_*.py`, `results/m4_probe.json`; `uv remove guidance` (and `pydantic` only if `grep` shows no use).
- **Rewrite:** `src/config.py`, `src/modal_server.py` (from the reuse map), `Makefile`, `.gitignore`. Add empty `src/prompts.py`.
- **Deps:** `uv add dspy datasets absl-py nltk langdetect immutabledict` (the checker's own `requirements.txt` lists absl, langdetect, nltk, immutabledict: verified). `matplotlib` is added at M1, `scipy` at M10.
- **Checker code:** copy Google's `instruction_following_eval/*.py` at one pinned commit into `third_party/instruction_following_eval/`, Apache-2.0 header kept, a `NOTICE` line with the commit hash. Not edited.
- **Because it sits outside `src/`:** ruff `extend-exclude = ["third_party"]`; pytest `testpaths = ["tests"]` (else pytest collects the vendored `*_test.py`) and `pythonpath = ["third_party"]`; `.pre-commit-config.yaml` top-level `exclude: ^third_party/` (else whitespace hooks rewrite Google's files); Makefile run targets use `PYTHONPATH=$$HOME/.pythoncustomize:third_party`; one `ci.yml` step downloads the nltk data (approved); the `wc -l` 300-line line is removed from `make lint` (approved).
- **Gate (stop and ask if it fails):** vendored `instructions_util.py` loads `nltk:tokenizers/punkt/english.pickle` (line ~135, verified), which recent nltk may refuse (assumed). Probe with one sentence-counting instruction. If it fails I show the error and options (one-line patch breaks "as is", wrap in `src/checks.py`, or older nltk); she picks.
- **Checks (each its own command, exit code read):** `uv run python -c "import langdetect, nltk, absl, immutabledict, dspy, datasets"` exits 0 on Python 3.14 (langdetect 1.0.9 has no 3.14 classifier, so this is a real test); `PYTHONPATH=third_party uv run python -c "from instruction_following_eval import evaluation_lib"` exits 0; `uv run pytest` exits 0; CI green on push.
- **Preflight (day 0):** Modal token works through the proxy; Gemini key name is present in `.env` (names only, never values); HF dataset download works (first used in M1).
- **Screenshot:** none. **Tests:** none (no logic).
notes: M0 done. Findings: (1) nltk 3.10.4 redirects the old punkt pickle to punkt_tab, so no patch; run make nltk_data once per machine, CI step added. (2) .env key is GOOGLE_API_KEY (pass api_key explicitly in M5). (3) Coverage gate failed with no imports of config.py; added a split-fractions-sum test. (4) Server rewrite moved to M3; modal_server.py keeps only kv_cache_mib. (5) No .gitignore change needed (/results already ignored).
